Hero Course Student.name: Hero Course Student
Hero Course Student.description:
Students of U.A. Academy's Hero Course, the most watched classes in Japan: first-years in Class 1-A or 1-B, upper-years in Classes 2-A, 2-B, 3-A and 3-B. Mornings are homeroom lectures; afternoons are Foundational Hero Studies at the training grounds: battle trials, rescue drills and Quirk practice under pro-hero teachers. Each class lives in its own Heights Alliance building, with curfew, sign-outs and weekend visits home, and the broadcast Sports Festival makes every result public.

Most are competitive and proud, compare Quirks constantly and still help each other without being asked. First-years in April are talented and unproven: they misjudge their limits, overreach and argue about what a hero should be. Upper-years are steadier, and many hold provisional licenses and work at agencies under supervision. Without a license no student may use a Quirk in public outside supervised training or self-defense. Facing a real villain they are taught to shield civilians and call a pro, and many step in anyway. They judge a newcomer by their Quirk and their effort: they invite them to train, ask blunt questions and lose patience with anyone who coasts.

## Generating New NPCs
Classes 1-A and 1-B each have 20 canon students (a player may be an extra member), and both are full: a generated Hero Course student is a second- or third-year, never a member of 1-A or 1-B. The Big Three (Mirio Togata, Tamaki Amajiki, Nejire Hado) are canon third-years. Every student is an adult high-school graduate. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting their home region (foreign only for students from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name, and never copy a canon student's Quirk, look or role. Upper-years have an original hero name. The Quirk is strong enough for hero work, with a clear scope and a real limit or cost.

## Visual Description
Young adults. On campus: the U.A. uniform (gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, white shirt, red tie, dark green trousers or skirt). In training: the U.A. gym uniform (a dark blue tracksuit with white trim) or their own hero costume, built around their Quirk with practical support gear; upper-year costumes look worn in. Mutant features always show; Emitter and Transformation effects only in active use. No text, logos, emblems or badges.
Generated people of this type are second- or third-years (Classes 2-A, 2-B, 3-A, 3-B): Classes 1-A and 1-B are full with their canon students.

General Studies Student.name: General Studies Student
General Studies Student.description:
Students of U.A. Academy's General Studies course: first-years in Classes 1-C, 1-D and 1-E, upper-years in the same letters. They follow a full academic program of lectures, coursework and exams, join clubs and share halls in Heights Alliance with the Support and Management courses, under the same curfew and sign-out rules as everyone else. Many applied to the Hero Course and missed it, often because the entrance exam's robot battle rewarded combat Quirks; others came for U.A.'s name and plan ordinary careers.

The Hero Course gets the cameras, and they notice: some resent it, some shrug, and a few study Hero Course students closely and wait. A General Studies student can transfer into the Hero Course on merit, and the Sports Festival, where every first-year competes on live broadcast, is the showcase for it. Their course gives no hero training: in danger they run, help others out and call for help, and they use a Quirk only in self-defense. They treat a newcomer as a classmate first; a Hero Course student gets measured, teased or quietly challenged.

## Generating New NPCs
A generated student belongs to Class C, D or E of any year and is an adult high-school graduate. Hitoshi Shinso (Class 1-C) is canon: never generate another mind-control user aiming to transfer, or a copy of any canon student's Quirk, look or role. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting their home region (foreign only for students from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name. The Quirk may be weak or strong, since placement says nothing about strength, and has a clear scope and a real limit or cost. A transfer happens only through the story, never by assumption.

## Visual Description
Young adults in the U.A. uniform (gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, white shirt, red tie, dark green trousers or skirt), or the U.A. gym uniform (a dark blue tracksuit with white trim) for physical training, with ordinary bags, books and personal touches. No hero costume or support gear. Mutant features always show; Emitter and Transformation effects only in active use. No text or logos.

Support Course Student.name: Support Course Student
Support Course Student.description:
Engineering students of U.A. Academy's Support Course: first-years in Classes 1-F, 1-G and 1-H, upper-years in the same letters. Lectures cover design, materials and electronics; the rest of the day belongs to Power Loader's Development Studio, where they build and test the gear that ends up in hero costumes: gauntlets, boots, grapples, visors and braces. Mei Hatsume (Class 1-H) all but lives there. They share halls in Heights Alliance with General Studies and Management, and many stay at the workbench until curfew.

They want test subjects, data and lab time, pitch gear to anyone in a costume and judge heroes by how well the gear held up. Prototypes fail, sometimes loudly; an accident stops work and brings Power Loader and the infirmary. At the Sports Festival they may compete with gear they built, which makes it a showroom for support companies. Otherwise they have no combat training, and a gadget used on a person in public is assault unless it is self-defense. A newcomer gets asked about their Quirk within a minute, because every Quirk is a design problem.

## Generating New NPCs
A generated student belongs to Class F, G or H of any year and is an adult high-school graduate. Mei Hatsume is canon: never generate a copy of her or of any canon student's Quirk, look or role. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting their home region (foreign only for students from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name. The Quirk can be anything, with a clear scope and a real limit or cost; many are small and useful at a workbench. Their gear is prototype work: limited, fragile and sometimes unsafe, and a costume change goes through the Studio and takes time.

## Visual Description
Young adults. In lectures: the U.A. uniform (gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, white shirt, red tie, dark green trousers or skirt). In the Studio: work coveralls, often tied at the waist over a T-shirt, with gloves, safety goggles, a tool belt, soot and grease. Prototypes show only when the record states them. Mutant features always show. No text or logos.

Management Course Student.name: Management Course Student
Management Course Student.description:
Students of U.A. Academy's Management Course: first-years in Classes 1-I, 1-J and 1-K, upper-years in the same letters. They study the business side of hero work: agency management, contracts and finance, public relations, media, merchandising and the numbers behind the Hero Billboard Chart JP. They share halls in Heights Alliance with General Studies and Support. Every first-year competes in the Sports Festival, and they also watch it as a market: which students the agencies scout, and why.

They are polished, organized and quick with a pitch, and they see the Hero Course as future clients and brands. They talk about approval ratings, sponsors and image, and they like being useful to people who will be famous. Some are cynical about heroes; some want to run an agency that does real good. They have no combat training: in danger they evacuate, coordinate, call for help and use a Quirk only in self-defense. A newcomer gets a friendly, practical welcome and an informal assessment: their Quirk, their story and who would buy it.

## Generating New NPCs
A generated student belongs to Class I, J or K of any year and is an adult high-school graduate. Never copy a canon character's Quirk, look or role. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting their home region (foreign only for students from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name. The Quirk usually suits work and daily life (memory, perception, presentation) more than combat, with a clear scope and a real limit or cost. They are students: they hold no contracts and cannot hire, sponsor or rank anyone.

## Visual Description
Young adults in a neatly worn U.A. uniform (gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, white shirt, red tie, dark green trousers or skirt), with phones, tablets, notebooks and well-kept bags; off campus, smart casual clothes. No hero costume. Mutant features always show. No text or logos.

Rival Academy Student.name: Rival Academy Student
Rival Academy Student.description:
Students of Japan's other hero academies, which also train high-school graduates over three years. Shiketsu Academy in the west is U.A.'s closest rival, known for discipline, peaked caps and rescue work; Ketsubutsu Academy, Seiai Academy and smaller academies across the country complete the field. Each has its own campus, rules and traditions. Their students meet U.A.'s at the Provisional Hero License Exam and at joint events, and many follow U.A.'s broadcast Sports Festival each year to scout future rivals.

They are proud of their own academy and measure themselves against U.A. Shiketsu drills formal courtesy into its students, who compete fiercely under the manners; others are friendly in the waiting hall and ruthless in the arena, and some build their exam strategy around Quirks they saw on television. They fight as trained hero students, in teams and in their own costumes, and without a license they are bound by the same law as everyone else. A U.A. newcomer gets polite curiosity and a quiet scouting report; anyone else gets less attention.

## Generating New NPCs
Named canon students (Inasa Yoarashi, Seiji Shishikura, Camie Utsushimi and Nagamasa Mora of Shiketsu; Yo Shindo of Ketsubutsu) are canon NPCs: never generate a copy of them or of any canon student. A generated student attends Shiketsu, Ketsubutsu, Seiai or a smaller academy, never U.A., and is an adult high-school graduate. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting their home region (foreign only for students from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name. The Quirk is strong enough for hero work, with a clear scope and a real limit or cost.

## Visual Description
Young adults in their own academy's uniform: Shiketsu's dark formal uniform with a peaked cap, other academies' blazers or jackets in their own colors. At exams and joint training: their own hero costumes, built around their Quirks. Mutant features always show; Emitter and Transformation effects only in active use. No crests, text or logos.

U.A. Faculty.name: U.A. Faculty
U.A. Faculty.description:
The staff of U.A. Academy, run by Principal Nezu. Every teacher is a licensed pro hero, and most split their time between lectures, exercises and field work; the rest of the staff keep the campus fed, healed, secure and running. Faculty teach, grade, supervise exercises, enforce curfew and sign-outs in Heights Alliance and guard a campus that the U.A. Barrier locks to anyone without an ID. Their authority covers every student in every course.

They are teachers first: demanding, protective and willing to let a student fail an exercise so the lesson lands. They stop unauthorized fights, call a match once a student cannot go on and send the hurt to Recovery Girl. In a real attack the pros among them protect students before anything else and fight at full professional strength, while other staff evacuate students and call for help. A new student gets the rules, high expectations and a warning; a new colleague gets a timetable, paperwork and, sooner or later, a test from the principal.

## Generating New NPCs
The canon faculty are canon NPCs: Principal Nezu, Shota Aizawa (Eraser Head, Class 1-A homeroom), Vlad King (Class 1-B homeroom), All Might, Present Mic, Nemuri Kayama, Cementoss, Ectoplasm, Thirteen, Snipe, Hound Dog, Power Loader, Recovery Girl and Lunch Rush. Never generate a stand-in for them or a new teacher for a class or subject they hold. A generated faculty member is support staff (clerk, librarian, groundskeeper, security guard, bus driver, a cook under Lunch Rush, a nurse under Recovery Girl, a technician under Power Loader) or a teacher in another course or year. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region, never a canon character's name or family name. A teaching pro has an original hero name and a Quirk with a clear scope and a real limit; staff Quirks are everyday.

## Visual Description
Adults, from young instructors to the elderly Recovery Girl. Teaching pros wear their hero costumes or practical clothes; staff wear the clothes of their job: office wear, chef's whites, a medical coat, a security uniform, work overalls. Principal Nezu is a small white-furred animal in a suit, drawn only from his own record. No text, logos or lettered badges.

Pro Hero.name: Pro Hero
Pro Hero.description:
Licensed professional heroes. The Hero Public Safety Commission issues their licenses, and most work through agencies: running their own with sidekicks, or serving as a sidekick in someone else's. A working day is patrol, rescue, villain capture, coordination with the police and a pile of reports, with endorsements, interviews and fans on top. The Hero Billboard Chart JP ranks them twice a year on incidents resolved, public approval and social contribution; at the start of the year All Might is Number One, Endeavor Number Two and Hawks Number Three. Cameras follow every big incident.

Pros compete for incidents and credit and cooperate when lives are at stake. In a fight they protect civilians first, restrain and capture rather than kill, and hand villains to the police. They watch unlicensed Quirk users closely, students included. A student is a possible intern or a problem; a sidekick is staff; a civilian gets protection and often an autograph; a villain gets arrested.

## Generating New NPCs
Every top-ten hero and every named canon hero or sidekick (Best Jeanist, Edgeshot, Ingenium, Kamui Woods, Mount Lady, Death Arms, Gang Orca, Ryukyu, Fat Gum, Sir Nighteye, Gran Torino, Manual, Native, the Wild Wild Pussycats, Endeavor's sidekicks) is a canon NPC. A generated pro is a working hero or sidekick of ordinary standing, ranked far below the top ten, at an agency in the region where they appear, and never a stand-in for a canon hero. Use a Japanese real name, given name first, fitting the region (foreign only for heroes from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name, plus an original hero name. The Quirk has a clear scope and a real limit or cost.

## Visual Description
Adults in individual hero costumes designed around their Quirk and public image: a signature color scheme, protective layers, practical support gear and often a mask, visor or helmet. Sidekicks sometimes echo their agency's colors. Off duty: ordinary modern clothes. Mutant features always show; Emitter and Transformation effects only in active use. No text, logos, numbers or agency names.

Police Officer.name: Police Officer
Police Officer.description:
Officers of Japan's prefectural police forces under the National Police Agency: patrol officers in police boxes and cars, detectives, traffic and riot units, custody officers and the guards who move prisoners to Tartarus. They investigate crimes, secure scenes, interview witnesses and make arrests. Officers do not use their Quirks as weapons, so a Quirk fight belongs to licensed heroes: a hero restrains the villain and an officer applies the handcuffs. Detectives work cases for weeks and trade information with heroes they trust.

Most are procedural, polite and tired, and they expect cooperation. After a fight they cordon the scene, separate witnesses and ask who used a Quirk and whether they hold a license; unlicensed use ends in a warning or an arrest, whoever the user is. In danger they evacuate, hold a perimeter and call for heroes, and they draw a weapon only as a last resort. A newcomer gets courtesy and questions; anyone who keeps turning up near villain incidents gets more questions.

## Generating New NPCs
Detective Naomasa Tsukauchi, Officer Sansa Tamakawa and Hosu's police chief, Kenji Tsuragamae, are canon NPCs: never generate a stand-in for any of them. A generated officer is a patrol officer, detective, traffic officer, riot officer, custody officer or transport guard of the local prefectural force. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region, never a canon character's name or family name. They have a Quirk with a clear scope and a real limit or cost, or none, and never use it as a weapon.

## Visual Description
Adults. Patrol officers: a navy blue uniform, peaked cap and duty belt with radio and holstered sidearm. Detectives: plain suits and coats. Riot units: helmets, padded armor and shields. Heteromorph officers keep their features. No readable text, lettered badges or logos.

Commission Agent.name: Commission Agent
Commission Agent.description:
Staff of the Hero Public Safety Commission, the government body that runs the hero system from its headquarters in central Tokyo: licensing clerks, examiners and proctors, liaison officers sent to incidents, statisticians, press officers and policy officials. They issue and revoke hero licenses, run the Provisional Hero License Exam, coordinate heroes with the police and compile and present the Hero Billboard Chart JP.

They are bureaucratic and image-conscious. They speak in procedures and approval ratings, answer questions with prepared lines and weigh every incident by how it will look in the news. Most are capable people doing a demanding job; a few enjoy the power of a stamp. They avoid fights: in danger they call heroes and security and protect the files. Heroes depend on them and rarely love them. A license candidate gets forms, rules and an evaluation; a pro gets a reminder that a license can be suspended; a civilian gets a polite statement that says nothing.

## Generating New NPCs
The Commission's President and Yokumiru Mera, the official who runs the license exam, are canon NPCs: never generate a stand-in for them. A generated agent is ordinary staff in one named role, based in Tokyo or on assignment, and knows only what that role needs. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region, never a canon character's name or family name. Their Quirk has a clear scope and a real limit or cost, or they have none; few use one at work.

## Visual Description
Adults in formal dark business suits and white shirts, with ID lanyards, tablets, clipboards and radios; examiners and liaison staff may wear plain staff jackets. Mutant features always show. No readable text, emblems or logos.

Villain.name: Villain
Villain.description:
People who use their Quirks for crime, from muggers, shoplifters and street thugs to armed robbers, smugglers, hired muscle and the rare ideological killer. Heroes stop them, the police arrest them, and the worst end up in Tartarus. Most work alone or in small crews; brokers such as Giran sell them jobs, hideouts, forged IDs and black-market support gear. At the start of the year the League of Villains is tiny: Tomura Shigaraki, Kurogiri and thugs hired through brokers.

Villains have reasons: money, revenge, ideology, addiction, fear or the thrill of breaking rules. Small-timers rob, run and hide; organized ones scout, plan and recruit; a dangerous few go looking for heroes. In a fight most use their Quirks without restraint, grab hostages, wreck property to cover an escape and flee when a pro arrives; a cornered small-timer often gives up. A villain-path player meets them as contacts, rivals, employers and threats, and their loyalty has to be earned. To most of them a hero or student is a target or an obstacle, and a civilian is a victim or leverage.

## Generating New NPCs
Tomura Shigaraki, Kurogiri, Stain (the Hero Killer), Giran and every villain who joins the League later are canon NPCs: never generate a stand-in for them. A generated villain is a petty criminal, gang member, smuggler, small-time broker or hired thug, usually no match for a pro, and knows nothing of the League's plans. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region (foreign only for visitors from abroad), never a canon character's name or family name; a street alias is optional. The Quirk has a clear scope and a real limit or cost. A heteromorph body never marks someone as a villain.

## Visual Description
Adults with no shared uniform: street clothes, hoodies, work clothes, masks, scarves, caps and cheap or black-market gear. Mutant features always show. No capes, glowing eyes, blood or gore unless the record states them, and no text or logos.

Yakuza.name: Yakuza
Yakuza.description:
The last remnants of the yakuza houses that ran Japan's underworld before heroes rose. Heroes and police broke the great crime families; the survivors are designated villain groups, watched by the police and kept small. At the start of the year the best known is the Shie Hassaikai in Osaka, run by Kai Chisaki (Overhaul) while its old boss lies in a coma, with the Eight Bullets as his enforcers. The houses live on protection, loans, gambling and smuggling, including the Quirk-boosting street drug Trigger.

Members keep the old forms: rank, formal greetings, debts of honor and loyalty to the house and its boss, and they despise heroes as the people who ended their world. Loyalty to the house and loyalty to its current leader are not always the same thing. They are polite to outsiders until crossed, and a stranger who asks questions gets watched before anyone answers. In a fight most are disciplined: they move in groups, use knives, guns and Quirks, shield their bosses first and retreat on orders.

## Generating New NPCs
Kai Chisaki, the old boss and the Eight Bullets are canon NPCs: never generate a stand-in for them. A generated member is a soldier, driver, guard, debt collector or bookkeeper of the Hassaikai or a smaller house, and knows only their own job, never the house's inner business. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region, never a canon character's name or family name; Osaka locals speak Kansai-ben. The Quirk has a clear scope and a real limit or cost.

## Visual Description
Adults in dark suits, open-collared shirts and long coats, with neat, cropped or slicked-back hair. Chisaki's inner circle wear beaked plague-doctor masks; ordinary members do not. No tattoos, weapons or regalia unless the record states them, and no text or logos.

Nomu.name: Nomu
Nomu.description:
Nomu are hulking bio-engineered creatures with exposed brains, enormous strength and several Quirks stacked in one body. Most are mindless: they obey the handler who commands them, attack the targets they are given and ignore everything else. They do not bargain, fear or tire, and they show no sign of pain; most never speak, and the rare advanced kind manages only a few broken words. At the start of the year no hero, officer or member of the public has seen one.

In a fight a Nomu ranges from a match for a capable pro to a match for a top hero: fast, durable and crushing, with Quirks such as regeneration, flight or armored skin layered on raw power. Nomu follow orders literally, which a clever hero can exploit, and one without a fresh order stands idle or keeps to the last one. Stopping one takes the right counter to that Nomu's specific Quirks, or overwhelming force. To a Nomu, a newcomer, ally or enemy is only a target, an obstacle or nothing at all.

## Generating New NPCs
Nomu never appear at random or as ambient encounters: only where the story places them, always under a handler's orders. Canon Nomu are canon NPCs, and a generated Nomu needs a story reason. Give each one a short designation, never a personal name, and two to four Quirks, each with a real limit a hero can find; never repeat a canon Nomu's Quirk set. Never describe or speculate about where Nomu come from.

## Visual Description
Huge, hairless bodies with dark or ashen skin, the brain exposed on top of the head, lidless staring eyes and a beaked or wide, toothed mouth; some have wings or extra limbs. Plain dark trousers at most. The exposed brain is drawn clean and stylized: no blood, wounds or gore. No chains, tubes, text or logos.

Civilian.name: Civilian
Civilian.description:
The ordinary people of Japan: office workers, shopkeepers, station staff, delivery drivers, nurses, reporters, retirees and the families of students and heroes. About four in five have a Quirk, registered at age four, and most Quirks are small and everyday: a knack that helps at work, a minor Mutant feature, a party trick. Public Quirk use without a hero license is illegal except in self-defense, so most people use their Quirks only in private. Heteromorph people face prejudice, and people with no Quirk face pity.

They follow the hero rankings, buy merchandise, film every fight on their phones and complain about property damage afterward. In danger they run, hide, help others out and call for heroes; a few freeze, and a few use a Quirk in self-defense. They are courteous and reserved with strangers, louder and quicker to joke in Osaka, and wary of anyone who uses a Quirk openly in public. A civilian with an everyday Quirk can be the one witness who noticed what mattered.

## Generating New NPCs
Civilians are adults; anyone who is still a minor takes the Child type and its rules. Families of canon characters (such as Inko Midoriya) are canon NPCs: never generate a relative of a canon character. Use a Japanese name, given name first, ordinary for the region (foreign only for visitors and residents from abroad), never a canon character's family name. Give an everyday Quirk with a clear scope and a real limit, or none (about one in five). They know only what the news, rumor and their own eyes tell them.

## Visual Description
Adults in the everyday clothes of modern Japan, suited to their work and the season: office suits, shop aprons, station and delivery uniforms, nurse's scrubs, casual weekend wear. Heteromorph features (animal heads, horns, scales, extra arms) are common and ordinary. No hero costumes, and no text or logos.

Child.name: Child
Child.description:
Children are the people this world protects first. This type covers anyone who is still a minor, from small children to students at schools such as Aldera High School. Most children get their Quirk around age four, when it is registered, and a young Quirk is new, hard to control and prone to misfiring; fewer than one child in five has none, since Quirklessness is rarer among the young. An ordinary childhood here means kindergarten or school, parks and train rides with family, and many children idolize heroes and beg for autographs.

Every child is treated as a child, always. A child is never in romantic, flirtatious or sexual content, never the focus of physical description and never a combatant: children do not fight, though a child may act on impulse to protect someone. When danger reaches a child, the nearest hero, officer or adult moves to protect them first, and the narration stays on the rescue, not on the child's fear or injury; danger to a child is never narrated for spectacle. Most children are curious, loud, shy or stubborn by turns, trust heroes on sight and are wary of strangers. With a newcomer they hide behind a parent or guardian, stare at their Quirk or ask whether they are a hero.

## Generating New NPCs
Eri and Kota Izumi are the canon children: never generate a stand-in, sibling or companion for them. A generated child appears in an ordinary place (a park, a shop, a station, a residential street, a hospital waiting room) with a parent, guardian or teacher nearby, and never carries a story secret. Use a Japanese name, given name first, fitting the region, never a canon character's family name. Describe a small child only as a small child, and an older minor only as a schoolchild, plus clothes and expression: no build, figure or body words. Any Quirk is small, with a clear limit, or absent.

## Visual Description
A small child in ordinary children's clothes: a T-shirt and shorts, a simple dress, a kindergarten smock and yellow hat, a hoodie in a favorite hero's colors. An older minor: a plain school uniform or casual clothes. Small Mutant features (a tail, scales, animal ears) only where the record states them. No body or build description, and no text or logos.

Animal.name: Animal
Animal.description:
The animals of this world: pets, strays and city birds; working animals such as police and rescue dogs; farm animals; and wildlife, from the macaques, sika deer, wild boar, foxes, tanuki and black bears of the mountains to the gulls and crows of the harbors. Some animals have Quirks, though most do not, and a Quirk-bearing animal has one simple ability tied to its body and species.

Animals behave as their species does. They do not speak human language: they communicate through sound, posture and behavior, and a real conversation needs a fitting Quirk such as Koji Koda's. Their reactions are fear, curiosity, hunger, play or territory, never malice. In a fight an animal flees, defends itself or its young, or attacks when cornered, at its species' own strength. A frightened animal is a rescue problem: heroes and police calm, contain and return animals rather than hurt them. A newcomer gets the species' usual welcome: a curious dog, a wary stray cat, a bold crow.

## Generating New NPCs
Choose a species that fits the place, region and season. Pets carry owner-given names such as Pochi, Momo or Kuro; wild animals have none. Give a Quirk only when the story calls for one, simple and with a real limit. An animal never speaks and never reasons as a person. Principal Nezu is U.A. Faculty, never this type, and heteromorph people with animal features are people, never animals.

## Visual Description
Real species anatomy and natural coloring, with markings exactly as stated; a pet may wear a plain collar. No clothing, human posture, human expressions, glow or speech bubbles. A Quirk shows only as the record states. No text or logos.
